# cycle_vpn (Resource)

Manages the VPN service for a Cycle environment. The VPN is an environment singleton — it always exists and has no create or delete HTTP resource. Create and update send a `reconfigure` job; destroy disables the service and removes the resource from state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The VPN is an environment singleton. This resource reconfigures the
# service that already exists on the environment.
resource "cycle_vpn" "api" {
  environment_id    = cycle_environment.api.id
  enable            = true
  high_availability = false
  auto_update       = true
  allow_internet    = false
  cycle_accounts    = true
  vpn_accounts      = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) The ID of the environment whose VPN is managed. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Optional

- `allow_internet` (Boolean) When `true`, routes all traffic through the VPN, including non-Cycle traffic.
- `auto_update` (Boolean) Whether the VPN service container is set to auto-update.
- `custom_directives` (String) Additional OpenVPN directives appended to the server configuration on service start. Each line should follow standard OpenVPN syntax.
- `cycle_accounts` (Boolean) When `true`, any Cycle account with access to the environment can log in to the VPN with their Cycle email and password.
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether the VPN service is enabled.
- `high_availability` (Boolean) Whether the VPN service runs in high availability mode. The GET VPN service payload does not return this field; Terraform keeps the last configured value after apply.
- `vpn_accounts` (Boolean) When `true`, custom VPN user accounts (see `cycle_vpn_user`) can log in to the VPN.
- `webhook` (String) Optional webhook URL used to authorize VPN logins. Cycle posts the supplied credentials and expects HTTP 200 to permit the login.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The environment ID this VPN belongs to. The VPN is a singleton keyed on `environment_id`.
- `url` (String) The URL associated with the VPN service.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The VPN is imported using the environment ID.
terraform import cycle_vpn.api 651efd54c53f7b6e2c5a9f21
```
